topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture on cancer evolution, summarizing previous concepts and outlining the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Darwinian Selection
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer explains how sequential genetic mutations provide competitive fitness advantages to drive clonal expansion across pre-malignant tissues.

topics.label: Epigenetic Regulation in Malignant Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer demonstrates how transient epigenetic reprogramming can trigger tumorigenic properties independently of permanent DNA mutations.

topics.label: Stem Cell Hierarchies and the Cell of Origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stem cell properties and cellular differentiation hierarchies influence tumor initiation and progression across blood and solid tissue models.

topics.label: Environmental Promoters and Inflammatory Signaling in Tumor Initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how external promoters and chronic inflammation create permissive microenvironments that enable mutated cells to transform.

topics.label: Stromal Dependencies in Established Tumors and Therapeutic Implications
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer explains the ongoing dependence of mature tumors on their surrounding stroma and the potential for microenvironment-targeted therapies.

topics.label: Technologies for Profiling Tumor Evolution and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer reviews single-cell sequencing and spatial omics techniques used to analyze cellular interactions and mutational histories in tumor tissues.

topics.label: Synthesis of Cancer Evolution and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics summarize the combined evolutionary contributions of mutations, stemness, epigenetics, and microenvironment before concluding the lecture.
